title: Move Zeroes
summary: Given an integer array nums, shift all zeros to the end while preserving the order of non-zero elements.
statement: Given an integer array nums, shift all zeros to the end while preserving the order of non-zero elements. Perform this operation in-place without creating a new array.
constraints: Move every zero to the end of the original list while preserving the relative order of nonzero values. Return nothing and use constant auxiliary space.
hints: Maintain the first position where the next nonzero value belongs.
Scan with a read index; when its value is nonzero, swap it into the write position and advance write.
Because write never passes read, each swap moves a nonzero forward and a zero toward the suffix.
Nonzero values are encountered and written in original order; no separate output list is needed.
editorial: The write pointer counts nonzero values already placed. Each new nonzero swaps into that next position. Since reads progress left to right, stable nonzero order is preserved, and every displaced zero eventually remains in the suffix. The independent oracle explicitly collects the nonzero subsequence and appends the exact number of zeros.

tests.explanation: The nonzero subsequence 1,3,12 keeps its order and the two zeros occupy the final positions.
The only element is already a trailing zero, so the list remains unchanged.
